configs.description: The AC build, back-to-front air: the fan module turned 180 degrees so that the blue AIR INLET label shows at the rear. Ordered as DCS-7010TX-48-R and DCS-7010TX-48C-R.

configs.description: The DC build, front-to-back air: two internal -48 V DC supplies on terminal blocks (a different rear), the fan module as in the AC front-to-back build. Ordered as DCS-7010TX-48-DC-F and DCS-7010TX-48C-DC-F.

configs.description: The DC build, back-to-front air: the DC rear with the fan module turned so that AIR INLET shows. Ordered as DCS-7010TX-48-DC-R and DCS-7010TX-48C-DC-R.

gaps.note: Guide Table 1 gives 25.8 cm deep; the data sheet gives 27.6 cm (10.8 in) "incl. fans". They are different measures, the second including the fan module's protrusion, and the guide's figure was modelled.
gaps.wanted: a mechanical drawing that dimensions the body and the fan module's projection separately.

gaps.note: Same measure (typical / maximum draw), same models, different values. Guide Table 3 (PDOC-00061-08): 75 W / 100 W for all four builds. Data sheet (03-0052-14): 7010TX-48 61 W / 80 W, 7010TX-48C 83 W / 95 W, 7010TX-48-DC 56 W / 75 W, 7010TX-48C-DC TBD. The device carries the guide's, the newer document.
gaps.wanted: the maker's statement of which is current, per part number.

gaps.note: Storage temperature -25 to 70 C (guide Table 2) against -40 to 70 C (data sheet), and relative humidity 5 to 90 percent against 5 to 95 percent. The guide's, the newer document, are in attrs.
gaps.wanted: the maker's statement of which is current.

gaps.note: The -48C part numbers differ from the 7010TX-48 in system memory (8 GB against 4 GB), minimum EOS release and the data sheet's power figures, and no configuration can state a device attribute (the same open gap as cisco/asr-9001). The attrs carry the 7010TX-48's and the platform memory line names both.
The guide's Figures 3-1 to 3-3 are isometric and carry no measure, and the kit guide for KIT-7010, KIT-7010-4POST and KIT-7010-2POST-23 is not held, so no ear position or rail kit is written.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned drawing of the mounting bracket position, and the kit guide.

gaps.note: The module's width and height are measured off the data sheet's rear photographs, and nothing states its depth or the length of its projection beyond the chassis, so the fan component states none and has no 3D body.
The guide's power tables and the data sheet give whole-switch figures only; the fan component's missing power figure (lint L27) stands.
The 7010TX-48-DC and 7010TX-48C-DC print "7010TX-48-DC" on the front; the one modelled front prints "7010TX-48". The difference is the legend alone.
gaps.wanted: a second front view for the DC builds; not drawn, to keep one front per face of this device.

gaps.note: The photographs' printed text in Chinese, the French lines of the warning box, the two-line "INPUTS (2)" legend in three scripts, the fine print of the bar-code stickers and the hand-and-fan pictogram are drawn only as far as the English words and the pictograms' outlines; the stickers are blank placeholders and no serial, MAC or part number is transcribed.

gaps.note: The management jack is drawn with common/rj45-eth@1, the library's only single Ethernet jack, which carries two corner lamps; the datasheet photograph shows none on the hardware, and no lamp-less single Ethernet jack exists in the library.
gaps.wanted: a lamp-less single Ethernet jack part, or a photograph that shows lamps the datasheet crop hides.

gaps.note: The two internal power supplies state no model, wattage or dimension in any document held, so no power output is stated for them.

chassis.note: Guide Table 1: 48.3 x 4.4 x 25.8 cm (19 x 1.75 x 10.0 in), 3.9 kg (8.6 lb), the same for the 7010TX-48, -48C, -48-DC and -48C-DC. The datasheet gives 17.3 x 1.71 x 10.8 in (43.9 x 4.35 x 27.6 cm) "incl. fans". The width: 48.3 cm is over the mounting ears, so the body between them, which is what is modelled, is the datasheet's 43.9 cm (439.0), a 22.0 mm ear each side. The height is the datasheet's 43.5 mm (the guide rounds it to 4.4 cm, which is also the 1RU 44.45 less clearance). The depth is the guide's 258.0: Table 1 gives 25.8 cm as the chassis depth, while the datasheet's 27.6 cm is stated "incl. fans" (Technical Specifications, Size row), so it is a different measure. The two are recorded in the `sources-disagree` gap `depth`, and the chassis depth is the one modelled. 1RU.

colour.note: The front is the median of 400 pixels of bare plate in the datasheet photograph, #9b9ea6; the rear plate is the median of the same on the rear photograph, #acb4b6.

configurations.note: Data sheet Ordering Information: DCS-7010TX-48-F and -R (2 x AC, front-to-rear and rear-to-front air), DCS-7010TX-48C-F and -R, DCS-7010TX-48-DC-F and -R (2 x DC PSU), DCS-7010TX-48C-DC-F and -R. The guide names the four power builds without the air suffix. The -48C builds are the same front panel, rear and fan; they differ in system memory (8 GB against 4 GB) and minimum EOS release (4.31.1 and 4.33.2 against 4.26.0) and in the data sheet's power figures, which a configuration cannot state (the open gap `config-scoped-device-attrs`). They are therefore part numbers of the same four configurations, not devices of their own. The 7010T-48 and -48-DC (Figure C-1) have a different front panel and the DCS-7010TX-48C-DC-RV3 and -RV3A builds a different chassis for ORv3 and MGX racks (their fan supports only the -F orientation); both are left for a later slice.

ears.note: NOT MODELLED. The guide's Chapter 3.1 ships two mounting brackets and six M4x5 flat-head screws for a two-post or four-post rack and shows them in Figures 3-1 to 3-3, which are isometric drawings that carry no measure; the datasheet lists the spares KIT-7010 (accessory kit), KIT-7010-4POST and KIT-7010-2POST-23. No figure measures the bracket position, so no ear position is written and no rail kit is listed in chassis.kits (the kit guide is not held). Recorded in the gap rack-ears.

environment.note: Guide Table 2: operating 0 to 40 C, storage -25 to 70 C, altitude 0 to 3,000 m, humidity 5 to 90 percent non-condensing. Data sheet: operating 0 to 40 C, storage -40 to 70 C, humidity 5 to 95 percent, altitude 0 to 3,000 m ("certain airflow configurations or ... higher power ... optics may reduce the maximum operating temperature"). Storage temperature and humidity differ: gap `environment`, the guide's used.

front-legend.note: The vertical model legend reads "7010TX-48" up the left edge (centre 13.7 mm down, baseline 5.3 mm across, cap height 2.5) with the maker's wordmark below it from 23.8 to 40.2. THE WORDMARK IS NOT DRAWN: a logo-zone region is reserved over it and the plain model text is set. The datasheet's DC front prints "7010TX-48-DC" in the same place; one front is modelled for both builds and the difference is the gap front-legend-dc.

front-ports.note: Figure C-2 and the datasheet photograph, 11.97 px per mm anchored on the 439 mm body. 48 jacks in two stacked rows, four shells of six columns. The white column dividers in the photograph read, from the left, 13.7, 28.0, 42.0, 55.9, 69.9, 83.9 and 98.2 mm in the first shell and the same plus 91.2, 182.3 and 273.5 in the next three, so the column pitch is 13.97 (the registry's 0.550 in ganged-jack pitch) and the shells are 91.17 mm apart, a 7.35 mm gutter between six-column groups. The first jack opening reads 14.7 to 27.6 mm from the left edge, so the first cutout is at 14.6 (centre 20.95). The upper row opening reads 12.2 to 22.1 and the lower 25.8 to 36.2 down, so the rows are centred 17.1 and 31.0 mm down, a 13.9 row pitch, and each 11.0 cell is placed to those centres. The shells (white plates) read 12.0 to 99.3 across and 10.6 to 37.2 down; the top row is the same part turned 180 so that its latch is up and its two lamps are above, as the photograph shows lamps above the upper jacks and below the lower ones.

fru-bays.note: Guide Appendix E: "Only the fan module is field replaceable." Chapter 4: "The switches operate with two internal power supplies. At least one of the supplies must connect to a power source." The data sheet calls them "integrated AC power" and "integrated DC power supplies". So THE POWER SUPPLIES ARE PART OF THE CHASSIS AND ARE NOT BAYS: the two inlets (or terminal blocks) and the two lamps are placements, and the fan module is the one bay. No wattage, part number or dimension is published for the supplies.

gate-1-front.note: THE FRONT PHOTOGRAPH PASSES. The datasheet's 7010TX-48 front is 5257 x 524 px for the 439 mm body: aspect 10.03 against the stated 439.0 / 43.5 = 10.09, within 0.6 percent, so it is near-orthographic and carries geometry at 11.97 px per mm (the width is the scale anchor). The 7010TX-48-DC photograph (5248 x 523) gives the same positions. Every front position below is a measure off it, good to about 0.3 mm; it is `estimated` because it is read off a picture and no dimension states it. The guide's Figure C-2 is the callout drawing only.

gate-1-rear.note: THE REAR PHOTOGRAPHS PASS. The datasheet's rear photographs are 5227 x 521 px (AC rear-to-front), 5251 x 525 (DC) and 5204 x 536 (AC front-to-rear), each the 439 mm body across: aspect 10.03, 10.0 and 9.71 against 10.09. The first two pass; the third reads 3.8 percent tall because it is cropped higher, so only its x positions (the fan module and the red label) are used from it, and its fan figures were checked against the first. Positions are measures off the pictures at 11.9 px per mm anchored on the body width, good to about 0.4 mm.

interface-names.note: Not printed and not modelled. EOS names the front ports Ethernet1 to Ethernet52 and the management port Management1; this is the vendor's convention and no held document prints it, so the names stay out of the file as a block and go here.

lifecycle.note: Searched 2026-10-22. Arista's end-of-sale notice "End of Sale of the Arista 7010TX-48 Switches" (22420, announced 2025-09-19) gives the last day to order as 2026-03-20 and the end-of-life date as 2031-03-20; the 7010TX-48-DC has its own notice (22421, https://www.arista.com/en/support/advisories-notices/end-of-sale/22421-end-of-sale-of-the-arista-7010tx-48-dc-switches). The search result stated that other 7010X models are not affected; the page itself was read through the search summary and not fetched, so the dates are as that summary gave them and the -48C part numbers' status is not confirmed.

mgmt-stack.note: Figure C-2 callouts 4, 8 and 9, Figure 4-4: the Ethernet management port (10/100/1000), the USB port and the RJ-45 console serial port (RS-232, 9600 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, one stop bit, no flow control; pinout Table 5), in one dark metal housing 410.1 to 427.2 across and 6.6 to 38.7 down. The management jack's opening reads 8.2 to 18.0 down with its latch up (so it is turned 180), the USB-A 20.0 to 25.6, and the console 27.5 to 38.3 with its latch down. The photograph shows no lamp on the management or console jack. The console is std/rj45@2; the management jack is common/rj45-eth@1, the library's single Ethernet jack, whose two corner lamps the photograph does not show (a gap, mgmt-lamps); both are centred on 418.65. The management symbol above the stack, the USB trident right of it and the "10101" console legend below are printed.

other-faces.note: No source draws the top, bottom or sides flat. The guide's installation figures are isometric (Figures 3-1 to 3-4) and the rubber-pad figure shows the underside with four indentations but no measure. Each carries an `empty` sentence.

port-lamps.note: Guide Appendix A.1.2, Table 7 and its note: "For RJ-45 ports, the LED on the left indicates link status, and the LED on the right indicates traffic on the port." Off is link down, green link up, yellow software disabled, flashing yellow failed diagnostics. The photograph shows the pair at the two keyway-side corners of each jack, green on the left and amber on the right. The lamps are the jack housing's corner windows (common/rj45-ganged-eth) and carry that component's default vocabulary. The guide says the SFP ports' lamp behaviour is the same as the RJ-45 ports'.

port-numbering.note: The photograph prints the numbers above the top row in pairs, one pair a column: "1" with an up triangle and "2" with a down triangle, and so on to "47 up" and "48 down", then "49 up", "50 down", "51 up" and "52 down" over the SFP block. The triangle points at the jack it numbers, so the odd port is the upper jack and the even port the lower, and the numbering runs down each column then across. The guide's Figure C-2 numbers them the same way. Each digit group ends 1.0 mm before its triangle, read off the 12x crop: the up triangle sits 4.05 left of the column centre and the down one 5.25 right of it, all on one baseline 9.6 mm down. The SFP legends are read the same way: triangles at 381.6, 388.3, 395.4 and 402.0. The EOS interface names are not printed on the metal and are not modelled.

power.note: Guide Table 3: typical / maximum power draw 75 W / 100 W for the 7010TX-48, -48C, -48-DC and -48C-DC; AC supply rating 100 - 240 VAC, 2.2 A, 50/60 Hz; DC -40 to -72 VDC, 2.5 A. Data sheet: 61 W / 80 W (7010TX-48), 83 W / 95 W (-48C), 56 W / 75 W (-48-DC), TBD (-48C-DC), typical measured at 25 C ambient with 50 percent load; typical input current 0.96 to 0.48 A AC and 2.5 A maximum at -48 V DC; efficiency 93 percent (Platinum) AC and 92 percent DC. The two documents state the same measures for the same models and differ, so this is a `sources-disagree` gap (power-draw); the device attrs carry the guide's figure, the newer document, and the data sheet's are in the gap.

rear.note: Figures D-2 (AC) and D-4 (DC) callouts, with the datasheet photographs at 11.9 px per mm, rear seen from behind with x = 0 at the left of the drawing. PS1 is the left and PS2 the right. AC: each inlet is an IEC C14 in a hex-shaped flange 50.8 x 23.8 with a screw at each end, centred 29.8 and 409.2 and 24.8 down (flanges 4.4 to 55.2 and 383.8 to 434.6); a status lamp sits under each supply at 29.6 and 408.6, 41.0 down, with the legends PS1 and PS2 beside them. DC: each supply is a two-pole terminal block under a clear cover and guards (8.4 to 50.8 and 388.4 to 430.8 across, 11.2 to 38.6 down) with a tapped grounding hole and the earth symbol above it. The fan slot is 175.0 to 265.0 across and 2.3 to 42.3 down. The hex vent field is 270 to 380 across and 2.6 to 29.6 down, with a lower step 270 to 350 across and 29.6 to 39.8 down, because the grounding pair sits on bare plate at its lower right. The grounding pair is two tapped holes 358.1 and 374.3 at 34.3 down, the guide's lug size being M4 x 0.7, on the 5/8 in pitch the library's pair component fixes (the photograph reads 16.2, 0.3 over 15.875, inside the half-millimetre of the read). The warning box, airflow pictogram and three bar-code stickers are measured the same way.

rear-fan.note: The fan slot is a seat for a 73 mm module longer than the module: a blue "AIR INLET" label band at its left end (175.0 to 185.0) and a red "AIR EXIT" band at its right (254.1 to 264.1) are printed on the chassis, and the module covers one. Back-to-front (-R): the module is at the right of the slot with the blue band showing. Front-to-back (-F): it is at the left of the slot with the red band showing (datasheet photographs; guide Chapter 2.1 and Figure A-3). Both bands, the module and its handle are in the component, whose `airflow` field a configuration sets. The guide names callouts for "airflow direction indicator label (active)" and "(inactive)" and says the labels, not the handle, carry the colour; no handle finish is stated, so none is set.

sfp-cages.note: Figure C-2 and the photograph. Four cages in a two-by-two block, ports 49 and 51 above 50 and 52. The shield around them reads 376.4 to 407.0 across and 9.8 to 37.1 down; the openings abut on the registry's 14.25 pitch (SFF-8433) from 377.4, and the rows are 15.0 apart (the registry's measured stacked-cage pitch) from 10.8, which closes on the shield's lower edge. A pale blue strip printed "25G" runs under them, 377.4 to 405.9 across and 36.4 to 38.1 down. Four lamps sit under the strip at 382.3, 387.2, 396.3 and 400.9 mm, 39.4 mm down, one per cage, read in the order of the numbers above them. The guide calls them "SFP25 ports" (Figure C-2) and "SFP+" in the data sheet's specification table; the cage is one footprint (SFF-8433 applies to SFP28 too) and the rate is 1, 10 or 25 Gbps.

sources.note: 7010 Series 1RU Quick Start Guide, Arista Networks, document PDOC-00061-08, 41 pages, PDF created 2025-10-06 (https://www.arista.com/assets/data/pdf/qsg/qsg-books/QS_7010_1RU.pdf): Table 1 (dimensions and weights), Table 2 (operating and storage), Table 3 (power draw and supply ratings), Chapter 2.1 (airflow orientation), Figures 4-1 and 4-2 (grounding), Table 4 (DC wiring), Figure 4-4 (front ports), Appendix A (status indicators, Tables 6 to 8), Appendix B (parts list), Appendix C (Figure C-2, the front panel of the 7010TX-48, -48C, -48-DC and -48C-DC), Appendix D (Figures D-2 and D-4, the AC and DC rear panels), Appendix E (the fan module, "Only the fan module is field replaceable"). 7010X Series Data Sheet, Arista Networks, 03-0052-14, 10 pages, dated Aug 20th 2025 (https://www.arista.com/assets/data/pdf/Datasheets/7010TX-Datasheet.pdf): the technical specifications and ordering tables and its straight-on photographs of the front (7010TX-48 and 7010TX-48-DC) and of the rear (rear-to-front AC, front-to-rear AC and DC), which are what every position below was read from. The guide's own panel figures are small low-resolution rasters (about 1.4 px per mm), used for counts, numbering and callouts only. Arista publishes no 3D or CAD model, and the Visio stencil set could not be fetched, so no drawing or model is held. No drawing, photograph or logo is copied into the library, only transcribed facts and new drawings. 7010T-48 (Figure C-1, a different front with SFP+ cages and two supply lamps) and the 7010TX-48C-DC-RV3 and -RV3A rack builds are in the same guide and are left for a later slice, as the guide describes.

status-lamps.note: Guide Appendix A.1.1, Table 6 and Figure C-2 callouts 5 to 7: a system status lamp (flashing green on power-up, green when all supplies and fans are normal, blue when the locator is active, red for a missing or failed supply or fan), a fan tray lamp (green normal, red inserted-but-failed or absent) and a power supply lamp (off not inserted or unpowered, green normal, red failed). Three lamps in a column at 430.1 mm, 7.7, 11.1 and 14.6 down, with the system glyph, a fan glyph and "PS" beside them at 436.2. The guide gives one power supply lamp on the front of this model (Figure C-2 callout 7); the two supplies also have a lamp each on the rear.

vents.note: The photograph shows two rows of 18 rectangular slots above the first jack shell (12.05 to 98.2 across, 1.1 to 3.5 and 5.0 to 7.3 down) and one row of 18 below it (39.5 to 41.9 down), and seven in each of two rows above, and two slots below, the SFP block (375.3 to 407.9). The slots are 3.4 wide on a 4.866 mm pitch (read as 4.86 from slots 1 and 2 in the 22x crop and checked at slot 18); each is a plain dark rectangle declared as a vent. No vent is drawn above or below the other three shells, as the photograph has none. On the rear the hex perforation is the library's generic vent pattern in a measured extent.
